subject: Cloud Computing
title: Heroku: The PaaS Pioneer
description: A micro-lesson that makes Heroku: The PaaS Pioneer usable.

hook.text: In 2007, three developers built a platform where you could deploy a web app with one command.

buildup.text: Heroku handled scaling, databases, and infrastructure. Developers just wrote code and pushed it.

discovery.text: Salesforce bought Heroku for $212 million in 2010, validating PaaS as a real business model.

twist.text: Heroku's simplicity came at a cost: limited customization and prices that climbed fast at scale.

climax.text: Heroku inspired a generation of platforms: Vercel, Render, Railway. The PaaS idea spread everywhere.

punchline.text: Heroku showed developers what 'just works' could mean.

quiz.question: What was Heroku's key innovation?
options: Letting developers deploy web apps with minimal infrastructure knowledge
Creating the first cloud storage service

details.summary: Heroku pioneered PaaS in 2007 by letting developers deploy Ruby apps with a simple git push. It popularized the concept that developers should focus on code, not servers, and influenced every PaaS that followed including commercial cloud offerings.
details.whyItMatters: Heroku proved that abstracting infrastructure could make developers dramatically more productive. Its influence shaped how every major cloud provider designed their PaaS offerings.
takeaways: Heroku launched in 2007 as one of the first PaaS platforms
Git push deployment became the standard developer experience
It influenced PaaS design across all major cloud providers

faq.question: Is Heroku still relevant?
faq.answer: Heroku remains popular for prototyping and small applications, but its market share has declined as AWS, Azure, and GCP PaaS offerings matured. Heroku's free tier was removed in 2022, and competitors now offer similar simplicity with more scalability.

faq.question: What did Heroku get right?
faq.answer: Heroku nailed developer experience: deploy with git push, scale with a slider, add databases with a click. It proved that developers would enthusiastically adopt platforms that eliminated operational toil, setting expectations for all cloud platforms that followed.
